stem: A 15-year-old with gender dysphoria attends with her mother and stepfather, both of whom support gender-affirming medical treatment, but her biological father who also has parental responsibility has not been consulted; what is the main unresolved issue?

options.text: Whichever adult attends the appointment can provide the necessary parental consent
The adolescent's agreement alone is enough if she appears Gillick competent
Consent should come from both parents or all people with parental responsibility
The stepfather's support replaces any need to consider other parental responsibility arrangements
Parental consent is irrelevant once the patient is 15

explanation: Consent should come from both parents or all people with parental responsibility. This is the unresolved issue because the biological father has parental responsibility but has not been consulted.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the notes do not say that any adult who attends can provide consent.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the pathway requires parental consent and the adolescent's agreement alone is not enough here.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because consent needs to come from both parents or all people with parental responsibility, and one person with parental responsibility has not been consulted.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a stepfather's support does not replace the need to consider all people with parental responsibility.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because parental consent is still relevant at age 15 for this treatment pathway.
